parts.text:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D plus probiotic co-supplementation lowered Beck Depression Inventory scores compared with placebo in women with PCOS.
Sentence: "Vitamin D and probiotic co-supplementation, compared with the placebo, significantly improved beck depression inventory [β (difference in the mean of outcomes measures between treatment groups) - 0.58; 95% CI, - 1.15, - 0.02; P = 0.04], general health questionnaire scores (β - 0.93; 95% CI, - 1.78, - 0.08; P = 0.03) and depression, anxiety and stress scale scores (β - 0.90; 95% CI, - 1.67, - 0.13; P = 0.02)."
Measured as: beck depression inventory score
Population: Women with polycystic ovary syndrome aged 18-40 years
Intervention: 50,000 IU vitamin D every 2 weeks plus 8 × 10^9 CFU/day probiotic for 12 weeks
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 60
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Over 5 years, vitamin D supplementation versus placebo made no significant difference in change in depression scores among all participants.
Sentence: "There was no significant difference in change in the knee symptoms, depression, and serum levels of IL6 and hs-CRP between both comparisons after 3 years of cessation of the clinical trial."
Measured as: depression scores
Population: Adults with knee osteoarthritis from the Hobart centre of the VIDEO trial, followed up 3 years after 2-year treatment
Intervention: Vitamin D supplementation for 2 years, followed 3 years after cessation
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 173
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

{
  "rationale": "Study A gave vitamin D combined with a probiotic and assessed symptoms immediately after 12 weeks in women with PCOS, whereas Study B gave vitamin D alone for 2 years to adults with knee osteoarthritis and measured outcomes 3 years after stopping treatment.",
  "verdict": "genuine",
  "reason": "intervention",
  "also_differs": ["population", "outcome_measure"],
  "detail": "co-treatment and timing: 12 weeks of vitamin D plus probiotic vs 2 years of vitamin D alone measured 3 years post-cessation"
}
